fit.gap_handling_summary: Gaps (no MLE title, no RAG/LLM, no MLOps tools, no own deployment) are handled honestly: the closest real experience is shown, the course project is labelled as such, and the letter states openly that work is batch-based rather than deployed APIs. GCP could have been named explicitly.

issues: No contact details (user chose to leave them out), which an employer would still need
Education lacks institution and dates (not in material)

ats.reason: Clean, well-sectioned text with every real matching skill searchable and nothing faked; only the cloud provider name GCP/Google Cloud is missing despite BigQuery and Vertex AI use.

issues: Company specifics come mostly from the job ad; little use of company culture (ownership, team-first, learning culture)
No explicit link to the payments/merchant domain beyond the ad wording
Somewhat dense metric repetition from the CV
strengths: Honest framing of the DS-to-MLE move
Clearly addressed to the correct role and company
No stale content from the earlier letter

spacing_issues: Cover letter occupies only about half the page with no header block
issues: CV has no contact line under the name

fluency_and_tone_issues: "makes this role a compelling next step" - subject is plural (focus ... and work), 'make' would be cleaner
"weekly BigQuery-scored XGBoost churn model whose retention targeting was validated" - dense

notes_facts_used: never deployed a model as an API (framed honestly)

requests.evidence: Both CV and cover letter exist

requests.request: I'd rather leave those details out.
requests.evidence: No contact details in the CV

evaluation.summary: Both documents are scrupulously honest: every claim traces to the portfolio, notes or earlier letter, the course project is labelled as learning, and the letter openly states that the candidate has not deployed model APIs. The CV is clean, one page and ATS-friendly, though it lacks contact details (by user choice) and does not name GCP. The fit to a 4+ year MLE role with RAG and MLOps requirements is inherently weak, which the outputs present honestly rather than hide. The cover letter is well targeted but uses little company culture beyond the ad.
